correctness.rationale: For the auxiliary integer pair, writing \(S=da,T=dc,G=db\) yields coprime \(a,b\) with \(a^2=b^2+c^2\), while harmonic integrality gives \(a\mid d\). The positive factors \((cx-a)(cy-a)=b^2\) imply \(c^2\le a+1\), whereas the Pythagorean factorization and \(b\ge2\) give \(c^2\ge a+2\). This proves the lemma for every \(x,y\ge2\). The three possible \(\Omega(n)\le2\) shapes are checked by exact identities; the two witnesses have computed integral means and \(\Omega=3\).

value.rationale: The simultaneous arithmetic/geometric/harmonic integrality condition defines a natural existing number-theoretic sequence. Its first nontrivial prime-factor multiplicity is a precise structural invariant; the theorem proves the exact minimum \(3\) with sharp witnesses, and a stronger integer-pair lemma explains why no unbounded squarefree semiprime can qualify. Neither the table nor either weaker single-mean condition implies this fact.
